title: A Whole Flower in One Line? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
A tomato, a brinjal and a potato: one is red, one is purple and one grows under the soil, yet all three come from the same plant family. Aarav knows water is H2O and asks: can a whole flower be written in one line like that?

You will see the fixed order botanists use to describe a plant, then the floral diagram with its mother axis and rings, and every symbol of the floral formula: Br, actinomorphic, zygomorphic, K, C, P, A, G, superior and inferior ovary, fusion and adhesion. Then we decode the formula of Solanaceae step by step while its floral diagram builds ring by ring, meet the family (potato as a stem tuber, berries, uses), compare brackets with the adhesion line, pause and think, write the formula of a makoi flower, look at the fusion exam trap, solve an original NEET pattern question, and finish with a recap card and three questions. This is Episode 47 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 Tomato, brinjal and potato
0:30 Describing a plant + the floral diagram
0:58 The code: one symbol per part
1:44 Decoding Solanaceae, ring by ring
2:30 The potato family: features and uses
3:05 Brackets vs line + pause and think
3:53 Worked example: the makoi flower
4:23 Exam trap: fusion or adhesion?
4:44 Practice question (NEET pattern)
5:07 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Families Fabaceae and Liliaceae. Why does a pea flower look like a butterfly?
